_doc: Reference brief for the ruined-wasteland-city prop/building batch (see docs/art/CITY_PROPS_BRIEF.md for the full research + sources). gen_city_props.py builds every prompt from this file; never hand-write a prompt that bypasses it. render_style 'upright' = floodkey-isolated CoverObject-style piece on a magenta bg (matches crate.png's iso box angle); render_style 'tile' = flat opaque top-down 2:1 diamond floor/decal (matches floor_metal.png), filename gets 'tile_' so pixelize3.py classifies it correctly.
style: pixel art, vibrant saturated colors, high contrast, arcade, bold clean shapes
palette: rust red, ash gray, toxic green accents, warning amber, steel blue, bone white, wasteland-worn NOT clean sci-fi
view_upright: isometric pseudo-3D box angle, front-left corner facing camera, a little of the top face visible, matching a single supply crate cover object
view_tile: flat top-down seamless 2:1 isometric diamond floor tile
bg_upright: solid flat gray background (see gen_city_props.py's 2026-09-10 fix comment - magenta bled into subject material colors, gray matches the already-proven character-sprite precedent)
base_negatives: blurry, jpeg artifacts, gradient, soft shading, photo, 3d render, text, watermark, multiple objects, cropped, frame, border, clean, shiny, pristine, sci-fi, alien
upright_negatives: scenery, landscape, sky, ground plane, floor, multiple buildings, full scene, seamless texture, tiled pattern, repeating pattern, wallpaper, filling the frame, edge to edge
_upright_fix_2026-09-10: First pass revealed 2 failure modes for 'wall'/'fence'/'sandbag wall' subjects: SDXL rendered them as an infinite full-bleed MATERIAL filling the whole frame (no actual background left to key out - the magenta cue got absorbed into the material's own color) instead of a bounded object floating on a background. Separately, round/repeatable objects (oil drum, barricade-of-barrels) rendered as a TILED PATTERN of many small copies instead of one object, and 2 subjects (debris pile, concrete barrier) picked up magenta AS their own material color. Adding 'single isolated object' framing to 'wall panel block' subjects did NOT fix it (re-verified, still full-bleed) - the word 'wall' itself carries an extremely strong architectural-texture bias in this LoRA that overrides bounding language. 'a pile of debris' subjects DID render bounded correctly, so the fix for every wall/fence/sandbag piece is to describe them as a bounded RUBBLE/SCRAP CHUNK (never the word 'wall' or 'fence'), which happens to still be exactly the right in-game shape (a chunk = a wall-run/corner/end-cap/window piece once placed edge to edge). Objects prone to material-color confusion get an explicit real color word; the negatives ban texture/pattern/frame-filling framing.
